questions.enonce_markdown:
An organic compound S reacted with ozone (ozonolysis) to give compounds Q and R. Both Q and R react with $\mathrm{NaOH/I_2}$ to produce a yellow precipitate with antiseptic smell. Q reacts with HCN to produce the compound $\mathrm{CH_3C(CH_3)OHCN}$ while R gives a silver mirror with Tollens reagent.

(i) Write the structural formulae and names of Q, R, S and the yellow precipitate

| Substance | formula | Name |
|---|---|---|
| Q | | |
| R | | |
| S | | |
| yellow precipitate | | |

(ii) Write equations to show the reactions of

Q with $\mathrm{NaOH/I_2}$

R with $\mathrm{H^+/Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ *[10 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reasoning.**

- The compound formed from Q and HCN, $\mathrm{CH_3C(CH_3)(OH)CN}$, is the cyanohydrin of **propanone**: HCN adds across $\mathrm{C{=}O}$ of $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$. So **Q is propanone**. It contains the $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ group, so it gives the iodoform test.
- R gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent, so it is an **aldehyde**; it also gives a yellow precipitate with $\mathrm{NaOH/I_2}$, so it contains $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH){-}}$ or $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$: **R is ethanal**, $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$ (the only aldehyde that gives the iodoform test).
- Ozonolysis cuts the $\mathrm{C{=}C}$ bond of the alkene S and puts $\mathrm{C{=}O}$ on each carbon of the double bond: S is $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{C{=}CHCH_3}$, which gives propanone and ethanal.
- The yellow precipitate with an antiseptic smell is **triiodomethane (iodoform), $\mathrm{CHI_3}$**.

**(i)**

| Substance | Formula | Name |
|---|---|---|
| Q | $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$ | propanone (acetone) |
| R | $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$ | ethanal (acetaldehyde) |
| S | $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{C{=}CHCH_3}$ | 2-methylbut-2-ene |
| yellow precipitate | $\mathrm{CHI_3}$ | triiodomethane (iodoform) |

**(ii)**

- Q with $\mathrm{NaOH/I_2}$ (the iodoform reaction):

$\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3} + 3\mathrm{I_2} + 4\mathrm{NaOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{CHI_3} + \mathrm{CH_3COONa} + 3\mathrm{NaI} + 3\mathrm{H_2O}$

(Check: C 3 = 1 + 2; H $6 + 4 = 10 = 1 + 3 + 6$; O $1 + 4 = 5 = 2 + 3$; Na $4 = 1 + 3$; I $6 = 3 + 3$.)

- R with $\mathrm{H^+/Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ (oxidation of the aldehyde to ethanoic acid; the orange solution turns green):

$3\mathrm{CH_3CHO} + \mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}} + 8\mathrm{H^+} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{CH_3COOH} + 2\mathrm{Cr^{3+}} + 4\mathrm{H_2O}$

(Check: charge $-2 + 8 = +6 = 2 \times 3$; O $3 + 7 = 10 = 6 + 4$; H $12 + 8 = 20 = 12 + 8$.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the reagents and reaction conditions necessary for the following conversions

(i) $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CONH_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2H_2}$ *(as printed)*

(ii) $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2OCH_2CH_3}$

(iii) $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}$ *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The product is printed incompletely ("$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2H_2}$"): it is read as **ethylamine, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$**, the amine with one carbon fewer than the amide. This is the **Hofmann degradation**: treat the amide with **bromine and aqueous sodium hydroxide (or potassium hydroxide), warm** (about 70 $^\circ$C):

$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CONH_2} + \mathrm{Br_2} + 4\mathrm{NaOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2} + \mathrm{Na_2CO_3} + 2\mathrm{NaBr} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$

(Atom check: C $3 = 2 + 1$; H $7 + 4 = 11 = 7 + 4$; N 1; O $1 + 4 = 5 = 3 + 2$; Na $4 = 2 + 2$; Br 2.) *If the product was meant to be propylamine, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2NH_2}$ (same number of carbons), the reagent would be lithium tetrahydridoaluminate, $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$, in dry ether, followed by water: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CONH_2} + 4[\mathrm{H}] \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2NH_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$.*

**(ii)** Intermolecular dehydration of ethanol: heat **excess ethanol with concentrated sulphuric acid at about 140 $^\circ$C** (distilling off the ether):

$2\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{conc.\ H_2SO_4},\ 140\,^\circ\mathrm{C}\ } \mathrm{CH_3CH_2OCH_2CH_3} + \mathrm{H_2O}$

(Alternative, Williamson synthesis: sodium ethoxide, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2ONa}$ (from ethanol and sodium), warmed with bromoethane.)

**(iii)** Treat the amine with **nitrous acid ($\mathrm{NaNO_2}$ and dilute HCl) at 0-5 $^\circ$C**, then warm: the unstable aliphatic diazonium salt breaks down, losing nitrogen and giving the alcohol:

$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2} + \mathrm{HNO_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} + \mathrm{N_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$

questions.enonce_markdown:
Use a chemical equation in each case to illustrate the various types of the following organic reactions:

(i) Electrophilic substitution

(ii) Free radical substitution

(iv) Nucleophilic addition

(v) Electrophilic addition. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Electrophilic substitution** - nitration of benzene (the electrophile is $\mathrm{NO_2^+}$):

$\mathrm{C_6H_6} + \mathrm{HNO_3} \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{conc.\ H_2SO_4},\ 55\,^\circ\mathrm{C}\ } \mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$

**(ii) Free radical substitution** - methane with chlorine in ultraviolet light (chlorine radicals $\mathrm{Cl\cdot}$ are the reactive species):

$\mathrm{CH_4} + \mathrm{Cl_2} \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{UV\ light}\ } \mathrm{CH_3Cl} + \mathrm{HCl}$

**(iv) Nucleophilic addition** - hydrogen cyanide with ethanal (the nucleophile is $\mathrm{CN^-}$):

$\mathrm{CH_3CHO} + \mathrm{HCN} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CN}$

**(v) Electrophilic addition** - bromine with ethene (the double bond attacks the polarised $\mathrm{Br{-}Br}$; the orange bromine water is decolourised):

$\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2} + \mathrm{Br_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_2BrCH_2Br}$
